extracted.intended_audience: general public, researchers, journalists, and policymakers interested in USAID and foreign aid policy
extracted.subtask_description: Extracting and summarizing USAID practices, conditions, oversight rules, and standards that govern the provision, selection, and monitoring of financial assistance and contracts.

rubrics_metrics.name: Form of financial assistance: non-reimbursable grants
rubrics_metrics.description: Financial assistance supplied cash to developing country organizations to supplement their budgets. Although USAID formerly provided loans, all financial assistance is now provided in the form of non-reimbursable grants.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Historical shift from loans to grants; relevant when evaluating eligibility and financial terms of USAID-funded projects.

rubrics_metrics.name: Emphasis on financial (government-to-government) assistance
rubrics_metrics.description: In recent years, the United States had increased its emphasis on financial rather than technical assistance. In 2004 the Millennium Challenge Corporation was created as a new foreign aid agency mainly restricted to providing financial assistance. In 2009, USAID realigned programs to emphasize financial assistance, referring to it as 'government-to-government' or 'G2G' assistance.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Shows programmatic preference and modality (financial transfers to governments) which affects how grants are structured, monitored, and evaluated.

rubrics_metrics.name: Contractor selection on a competitive and objective basis
rubrics_metrics.description: Although USAID officially selects contractors on a competitive and objective basis, watchdog groups and others have occasionally accused the agency of allowing the bidding process to be unduly influenced by political and financial interests.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Criterion for evaluating procurement integrity; guidance includes scrutiny for political ties or non-competitive, non-objective awards (examples cited under Bush administration Iraq contracts).

rubrics_metrics.name: NGO anti-terrorism certification requirement
rubrics_metrics.description: USAID required NGOs to sign a document renouncing terrorism as a condition of funding.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Used as a funding condition and criticized as politically conditioned funding (statements from Palestinian NGO representatives cited). Relevant when assessing conditionalities attached to grants.

rubrics_metrics.name: Requirement to explicitly oppose prostitution and sex trafficking (grant condition)
rubrics_metrics.description: A 2003 law provided U.S. government funds via USAID grants with one of the conditions being a requirement to have 'a policy explicitly opposing prostitution and sex trafficking'.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Legal and constitutional context: in 2013 the U.S. Supreme Court ruled in Agency for International Development v. Alliance for Open Society International, Inc. that the requirement violated the First Amendment's prohibition against compelled speech. Important for assessing legally permissible grant conditions.

rubrics_metrics.name: Vetting and oversight to prevent funds benefiting terrorists
rubrics_metrics.description: Inspector General reports and internal vetting (e.g., USAID's Vetting Support Unit) are used to screen grantees and to assure that distributed funds 'do not benefit terrorists and their supporters'.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: OIG warned that staffing cuts/furloughs limited the agency's ability to perform these assurances; investigations (e.g., into HHRD) illustrate vetting processes and their scrutiny.

rubrics_metrics.name: Use of non-career (short-term) contracts for specialist services
rubrics_metrics.description: USAID frequently contracted with private firms or individuals for specialist services lasting from a few weeks to several years rather than assigning tasks to career U.S. government employees.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Context: historical staffing reductions and program expansion drove use of outside experts; relevant when evaluating appropriateness, continuity, and oversight of contracted work.

rubrics_metrics.name: Conditionalities tied to aid (e.g., coca eradication, 'terrorist-free zones')
rubrics_metrics.description: Some USAID funding in certain programs was conditional on actions such as farmers eradicating coca plants or participating communities declaring themselves 'terrorist-free zones' as required by U.S. law.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Examples (Bolivia) show how conditionalities can generate local resistance and political controversy; use this criterion to assess social and political acceptability of grant conditions.

rubrics_metrics.name: Standard harmonisation in public–private partnerships
rubrics_metrics.description: In public–private partnerships (for example, USAID's MOU with the Global Food Safety Initiative), work on benchmarking and 'standard harmonisation' aims to foster mutual acceptance of recognized certification programmes for the industry.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Relevant when grants/programs involve industry standards and certification: promotes interoperability and mutual acceptance across jurisdictions/partner organizations.

rubrics_metrics.name: Inspector General oversight and anti-corruption investigations
rubrics_metrics.description: The Office of Inspector General investigates alleged misuse of funds, terror-linked funding, and corruption (examples include a 2023 OIG investigation into a $110,000 award and a 2025 bribery scheme involving manipulation of contracting worth ~$550 million).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: OIG findings and criminal prosecutions are used to evaluate accountability, contractual integrity, and corrective action; monitoring OIG reports is essential for assessing program risk.

rubrics_metrics.name: Avoidance of financial conflicts of interest / minimizing funds returning to donor countries
rubrics_metrics.description: Reports have found that a substantial portion of aid money (e.g., ~40% in Afghanistan) returned to donor countries through corporate profits, consultants' salaries, and other costs, raising concerns about financial conflicts of interest.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Criterion for assessing value-for-money and whether aid expenditures predominantly benefit recipients vs. contractors/donor-country entities. Examine procurement practices and local content requirements.

rubrics_metrics.name: Alignment of aid with U.S. foreign-policy and stated development goals
rubrics_metrics.description: USAID states that U.S. foreign assistance has the twofold purpose of furthering America's foreign policy interests in expanding democracy and free markets while improving the lives of citizens of developing countries; official goal sets (e.g., 2004 White Paper) include strengthening fragile states, disaster relief, and poverty relief.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Used to evaluate program selection and prioritization: grants are assessed for alignment with both U.S. strategic interests and humanitarian/development objectives.
